en.title: Fairgame$ Officially Delayed to 2026 Amidst Development Woes
en.summary: After years of silence and rampant cancellation rumors, Haven Studios' ambitious heist shooter **Fairgame$** has officially been pushed back to 2026. While the game isn't scrapped, significant internal challenges have reshaped its development trajectory.
en.body:
For three long years, **Fairgame$** has been a ghost in the PlayStation ecosystem. Announced with a flashy CGI trailer at the 2023 PlayStation Showcase, the competitive multiplayer shooter from **Haven Studios** promised a thrilling blend of heists and PvP action. Players were set to infiltrate opulent mansions, pulling off daring raids while fending off rival crews. However, after that initial reveal, silence descended, punctuated only by whispers of internal turmoil and development struggles. Now, the speculation can finally be put to rest: **Fairgame$** has not been cancelled, but it has been officially delayed to 2026.

The news comes after a period of intense rumor and confusion, with some analysts even misinterpreting the situation as a full cancellation. However, industry insiders like **Jeff Grubb** have confirmed that the game is still in active development, merely shifted to a later release window. This delay appears to be a direct consequence of recent playtesting feedback. A spokesperson for PlayStation confirmed to Bloomberg that internal tests revealed "mixed" player feedback and retention results that "fell short of the goals we had set." Coupled with the "challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre," this led to the difficult decision to cease development as originally planned.

## A Rocky Road to Release

**Fairgame$** has faced a series of significant setbacks since its inception. The departure of studio founder **Jade Raymond** in May 2025, followed by director **Daniel Drapeau** several months later, signaled growing instability. Reports and rumors painted a picture of a game struggling with its core gameplay loop, with speculation about extraction modes and comparisons to titles like **The Division** and **Fortnite**. One pre-alpha playtest, in particular, reportedly did not go well, seemingly sealing the shooter's fate for its originally intended release window. Despite these challenges, the studio itself, **Haven Studios**, is reportedly not at risk of shutdown, and employees will not face layoffs. Instead, the Montreal-based team will pivot to a support role for other PlayStation projects while continuing work on **Fairgame$**.

## What This Means for Fans

For the passionate fans who have held onto hope for **Fairgame$** since its reveal, this news is a mix of relief and continued anticipation. The initial silence and persistent rumors of cancellation understandably created anxiety. Knowing the game is still alive, albeit delayed, is a positive step. However, the admission of "mixed" player feedback and shortfalls in retention goals raises questions about whether the core concept can truly resonate in a crowded live-service market. The PvP shooter genre is notoriously difficult to break into, with established giants and ambitious newcomers constantly vying for player attention. The success of **Fairgame$** will hinge on its ability to refine its gameplay and offer a truly compelling, unique experience that can capture and retain a dedicated community.

## What's Next

While an exact release date in 2026 has not yet been announced, the shift to a spring 2026 target indicates that **Haven Studios** is taking the necessary time to address the feedback and refine the game. Players should keep an eye out for future updates from PlayStation and **Haven Studios** regarding gameplay reveals and potential beta tests as the development progresses towards its new launch window.

content_raw: After its announcement years ago and no gameplay or updates ever since, Haven Studios’ Fairgame$ has been cancelled. While you may think this is bad news for the Montreal-based studio, a PlayStation spokesperson told Bloomberg there wouldn’t be any layoffs and that it would instead serve as a support studio. Where it will be assigned next remains to be seen, but it’s clear Fairgame$ wasn’t working. Its last test in particular seemingly sealed the shooter’s fate, as PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle told employees in an alleged email. “While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.” Announced at the 2023 PlayStation Showcase for PS5 and PC, Fairgame$ was touted as a competitive multiplayer shooter with heist elements. Players would infiltrate millionaires’ properties and attempt to score big while evading rival crews. A job listing claimed it was “on track to deliver a triple-A multiplayer experience,” but it faced several internal delays. In May 2025, studio founder Jade Raymond departed . Several months later, director Daniel Drapeau followed . Rumors circulated about the gameplay loop and how it incorporated elements from The Division and Fortnite . At one point, it reportedly had an extraction mode , but the following pre-alpha playtest apparently didn’t go down well . All in all, an expected outcome for Sony’s live-service initiative, which has been rife with cancellations, underperforming titles like Marathon , and the ill-received Horizon Hunters Gathering . What this entails for the publisher’s remaining efforts remains to be seen, so stay tuned for further updates.
